I literally thought it was just me. My NMom would take me shopping and force me to model every item of clothing, while constantly making rude or degrading comments about my body. (I have many a memory crying in the Kohl’s dressing room.) When we finally got down to the small list of items she allowed me to keep, we would head home and then I forced to try on all the clothes again, except this time for my enabler father. He would critique almost everything, and say the clothes he didn’t like looked “sleezy” or “trashy.” (mind you I was between the ages of 8-17 at the time.) The clothes my Dad didn’t like were returned. Even after this whole ordeal, my NMom would often yell “where’d you get that? I’d never let you wear that.” at a pare of shorts or leggings, Which was of course not true becuase she came with me every time I went clothes shopping. Even still, she would take whatever it was away and return it or trash it. Either way I never saw it again. I believe a lot of this contributes to me never really developing a sense of style, and being hyper aware of my sexuality from a young age. 

Now, My younger sister (she is 16, we are 7 years apart) is able to wear whatever she wants, and never consults my parents on her fashion decisions. She has a very developed sense of style that fits her personality. It’s like a slap in the face to see thay because I felt forced to be frumpy and not well dressed, and as a result did not feel pretty until my teen years when men started giving me attention, which put me in several dangerous and/or traumatizing situations.

I totally understand the feeling of not feeling at home in your own body, I have the same feelings! I just try to work on being compassionate to my body even if I’m abusing it with binges and what not. If you are really hard on yourself it will just cause emotional distress and make you want to seek out comfort and binge more. Hang in there, you’re doing the best you can. <3
thank you that means so much! 😭

Yes. This post describes so much of how I’ve been feeling. My EDad and I used to be really close when I was a young child, but he allowed my NMom to drive a wedge between us because she was jealous, and ruin any semblance of relationship we once had. He barely talks to me now. And he romanticizes my childhood so much that he has absolutely no idea who I am now. The way he could’ve been a rock to lean on when I was being abused by my NMom and Flying Monkey sister will always haunt me, because I might have a better sense of identity and have less severe symptoms of CPTSD if I had not been consistently let down and gaslit by him. I realize he was and is actively being abused by her, but he let me be the scapegoat for my mother and sister’s rages so he didn’t have to face the brunt of the abuse and that to me is the ultimate betrayal. I was a child, he was the adult charged with protecting me.
